purpose_background.quote: In accordance with ESSB 6260 (2026) and RCW  28A.300.072, OSPI is proposing to amend chapter 392-425 WAC to adopt permanent rules authorizing local education agencies to charge sliding scale fees for enrollment in the transition to kindergarten (TK) program and to establish rules related to the allocation of state funding for TK programs.
purpose_background.purpose: two stated aims: (1) authorize sliding scale fees for TK enrollment; (2) establish rules on allocation of state TK funding

purpose_background.quote: Permanent rule adoption is necessary to implement statutory changes enacted by the Washington state legislature, and to ensure school districts, charter schools, and state-tribal education compact schools have the rules and guidance necessary for implementation during the 2027-28 school year, including enrollment, budgeting, and program planning timelines.
purpose_background.fact: necessity rationale; affected entity types named (school districts, charter schools, state-tribal education compact schools); target school year 2027-28

purpose_background.quote: Permanent rules are necessary to implement ESSB 6260 (2026) in time for the 2027-28 school year.

Local education agencies require timely rules regarding sliding scale fees and state funding allocation criteria in order to conduct enrollment, staffing, budgeting, and program planning activities prior to the start of the school year.
purpose_background.fact: LEA planning activities said to depend on the rules: enrollment, staffing, budgeting, program planning

purpose_background.quote: Delayed adoption would create uncertainty regarding program administration and funding distribution and could impair implementation of legislatively enacted requirements.

Reasons Supporting Proposal: OSPI is proposing permanent amendments to chapter 392-425 WAC to implement ESSB 6260 (2026) and RCW  28A.300.072, including rules that allow local education agencies to charge sliding scale fees for TK and establish criteria for state funding allocations. Timely rule adoption is needed so districts, charter schools, and state-tribal education compact schools can plan for enrollment, staffing, budgeting, and implementation for the 2027-28 school year.

wac_392_425_040.quote: (1) Children meeting the following criteria are eligible to participate in a transition to kindergarten program offered by an eligible local education agency:
wac_392_425_040.fact: eligibility lead-in; program offered by an 'eligible' LEA
wac_392_425_040.uncertainty: LEA eligibility not defined in supplied text

wac_392_425_040.quote: (a) A child who has been determined, by the local education agency, to benefit from additional preparation for kindergarten through a screening process and tool; and
wac_392_425_040.conditions: screening process and tool; joined to (b) by 'and'

wac_392_425_040.quote: (b) A child who is at least four years old by August 31st of the school year in which they enroll in a transition to kindergarten program.
wac_392_425_040.conditions: age at least four by August 31st of enrollment school year

wac_392_425_040.quote: (2) In determining student eligibility and admitting students to a transition to kindergarten program, local education agencies must:
(a) Give priority to children most in need of additional preparation to be successful in kindergarten, as demonstrated through a screening process and tool.
(b) Give priority to children with the lowest family income not otherwise eligible and not enrolled in another local program.
wac_392_425_040.uncertainty: 'not otherwise eligible' referent not specified in text

wac_392_425_040.quote: (c) Not exclude, nor establish a policy to prohibit from participation, an eligible child due only to the presence of a disability.

(d) ((Not charge tuition or other fees from state-funded eligible students for enrollment in a transition to kindergarten program))Eligible local education agencies are authorized to charge sliding scale fees for enrollment in a transition to kindergarten program, except that no fee may be charged for the following:
wac_392_425_040.fact: double-parenthesized text concerns a prohibition on tuition/fees from state-funded eligible students; following text authorizes sliding scale fees with exceptions
wac_392_425_040.modality: permissive ('are authorized') with prohibition for listed groups ('no fee may be charged')
wac_392_425_040.uncertainty: see UI-05; the double-parenthesized text has no space before the following text; the permissive sentence is grammatically a stand-alone sentence despite sitting under the 'must:' lead-in (UI-07)

wac_392_425_040.quote: (i) Children who are eligible for but not yet placed in the early childhood education or assistance program or the head start program;
wac_392_425_040.conditions: eligible for, but not yet placed in, ECEAP or Head Start

wac_392_425_040.quote: (ii) Children with disabilities entitled to a free appropriate public education in accordance with the federal individuals with disabilities education act and chapter  28A.155 RCW.
wac_392_425_040.conditions: entitled to FAPE under IDEA and chapter 28A.155 RCW

wac_392_425_040.quote: (e) Tuition and fees collected for students in classrooms receiving state funding for the transition to kindergarten program must be accounted for separately, in accordance with the requirements outlined in the school district accounting manual.
wac_392_425_040.conditions: applies to tuition and fees for students in classrooms receiving state TK funding; standard is the school district accounting manual
wac_392_425_040.uncertainty: whether (e) is new or pre-existing text is not determinable from plain text (UI-06)

wac_392_425_065.quote: State funding for the transition to kindergarten program will be allocated to eligible local education agencies based on RCW  28A.300.072 and the state omnibus budget requirements. Funding allocations will be prioritized as follows:
wac_392_425_065.fact: allocation basis is RCW 28A.300.072 and state omnibus budget requirements; prioritization list follows

wac_392_425_065.quote: (1) Eligible local education agencies that received state funding allocations for transition to kindergarten in the previous year will have priority for the subsequent year.
wac_392_425_065.conditions: received state TK funding in the previous year
wac_392_425_065.uncertainty: 'previous year' / 'subsequent year' reference frame not defined

wac_392_425_065.quote: (2) When state funding is insufficient to maintain the number of students served in the subsequent year, eligible local education agencies will be allocated funding based on one or more of the following criteria:
wac_392_425_065.conditions: triggered when state funding is insufficient to maintain the number of students served
wac_392_425_065.modality: conditional, declarative future; 'one or more' criteria
wac_392_425_065.uncertainty: list ends with 'and' before (e) while lead-in says 'one or more' (UI-09)

wac_392_425_065.quote: (a) Districtwide percentage of students eligible for free and reduced price lunch;
(b) Districtwide percentage of students eligible for special education services;
(c) Districtwide percentage of students eligible for transitional bilingual program services;
(d) Data available measuring access to state-funded early learning programs; and
(e) Local education agencies serving 20 or fewer transition to kindergarten students.
wac_392_425_065.uncertainty: (e) is a category of LEA rather than a 'percentage' or 'data' measure like (a) through (d); how it operates as a criterion is not stated

proposed_rule_functions.function: Replace fee prohibition with authorization for eligible LEAs to charge sliding scale fees for TK enrollment
proposed_rule_functions.uncertainty: replacement reading depends on UI-05; 'sliding scale' not defined in text

proposed_rule_functions.function: Prohibit any fee for two child groups: ECEAP/Head Start eligible-but-unplaced children, and children with disabilities entitled to FAPE
Require separate accounting of tuition and fees for students in state-funded TK classrooms per the school district accounting manual
Establish allocation basis for state TK funding (RCW 28A.300.072 and omnibus budget) with priority for LEAs funded in the previous year

When funding is insufficient to maintain students served, allocate using one or more of five listed criteria (FRL percentage, special education percentage, transitional bilingual percentage, early learning access data, LEAs serving 20 or fewer TK students)
Retain student eligibility criteria (screening-based benefit determination; age four by August 31st) and admission priorities/non-exclusion rules as printed
proposed_rule_functions.uncertainty: whether these are unchanged cannot be confirmed from plain text (UI-06)

R040-2d's permissive sentence ('Eligible local education agencies are authorized...') sits under the mandatory lead-in 'local education agencies must:' in (2). The directive force of (d) as a whole is ambiguous between permission and a mandatory framing.

The double-parenthesized text refers to 'state-funded eligible students'; the authorization text refers to 'enrollment in a transition to kindergarten program' without that qualifier; (e) refers to 'classrooms receiving state funding'. Scope relationship among these phrases is not resolved by the text.
R065-2 says 'one or more of the following criteria' but the list is joined with 'and' before (e).
Terms not defined in supplied text: 'eligible local education agency', 'sliding scale fees', 'previous year'/'subsequent year', 'screening process and tool', 'another local program'.
